items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: My brother... played with different bands around here like Lewis, you know, and Kid René and all of them. And I just took the style behind him, pick it up behind him.

ctx.x: Your younger brother, you still have another young...

Yeah, Simon Fraser. Yeah, he's living with my second oldest sister, yeah. Yeah. I think it's in the 26th... No, the 2500 Dumaine Street. He was in... That's the one... He allowed him how to play the piano to, Simon Fraser, yeah. And... Let's see, we have... Like I first said, I started... Now, my oldest brother, and Paul Barberin, another old drummer, they all started by Amarico's Woodyard on North Ramport Street years ago. And Sam, he played with Kid René and part with Louis Armstrong, before Louis ever think…
Did you...when you took up drums, did you have any lessons? Did your father help you or any...

items.title: Percy Humphrey Band: Percy Humphrey, Jim Robinson, Ernest Roubleau, Josiah Frazier Interview, 1972-02-29
items.q: Rick, I was playing with him that Sunday.

ctx.x: . . . . . . . It was 21, street they called Corner and Roman. It was like you said, two, that time they had wagons. It was Punch with his band and Kid Rene with his band, but he happened to have two corners. Rick, I was playing with him that Sunday. And the first number they played, I was just, I think it was Panama. And then they came back and Punch picked up a good blues number. No, I don't think nobody in the world them days could beat Punch playing a blues number. Couldn't beat that man with a blues number.…
I know where it comes from, but I never know it being orchestrated. But the boys got the number. The boys got the number. The boys got the number. You want to bring out. I know that.
